items.title: Q1 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which among the following is not a type of meaning in a poem as defined by I.A. Richards in Practical Criticism?
items.explanation: In Practical Criticism (1929), I.A. Richards identifies four kinds of meaning that operate together in poetic language: Sense, Feeling, Tone, and Intention. "Form" is not one of these four communicative functions.

items.title: Q2 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
What is the correct sequence of various periods of English Literature?
A. Caroline Age
B. Jacobean Age
C. Restoration Age
D. Commonwealth Period
E. Augustan Age
items.explanation: The historical sequence of English literary eras is: Jacobean Age (1603–1625), Caroline Age (1625–1649), Commonwealth Period (1649–1660), Restoration Age (1660–1700), and Augustan Age (1700–1745). This gives the sequence B, A, D, C, E.

items.title: Q3 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem: Which of the following works is not written by Chinua Achebe?
items.explanation: Weep Not, Child (1964) is the celebrated debut novel of Kenyan author Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o. The other three works—No Longer at Ease (1960), Arrow of God (1964), and the essay An Image of Africa (1977)—were all written by Nigerian author Chinua Achebe.

items.title: Q4 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Name the British poet who wrote Sohrab and Rustum :
items.explanation: "Sohrab and Rustum" (1853) is a famous narrative poem in blank verse by Victorian poet Matthew Arnold. It recounts the tragic Persian legendary duel from Ferdowsi's Shahnameh between the warrior Rustum and his unrecognized son Sohrab.

C. William Wycherley
D. George Bernard Shaw
E. John Millington Synge
items.explanation: Arranged by birth year: John Dryden was born in 1631, William Wycherley in 1640, William Congreve in 1670, George Bernard Shaw in 1856, and John Millington Synge in 1871. This establishes the sequence B, C, A, D, E.

items.title: Q6 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
From the following writers, who are known for Magic Realism?
A. R.K. Narayan
B. Salman Rushdie
C. V.S. Naipaul
D. Gabriel Garcia Marquez
E. Mulk Raj Anand
items.explanation: Salman Rushdie (notably in Midnight's Children) and Gabriel García Márquez (notably in One Hundred Years of Solitude) are two of world literature's most celebrated exponents of magic realism (B and D). R.K. Narayan, V.S. Naipaul, and Mulk Raj Anand are realist writers who do not write in the magic realist mode.

items.title: Q7 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem: Who among the following African writers observed that “O my body, make of me always a man who questions”?
items.explanation: "O my body, make of me always a man who questions!" is the famous concluding line of Frantz Fanon's influential anti-colonial study Black Skin, White Masks (1952). Fanon concludes his work with this personal prayer for radical critical consciousness and liberation from racial prejudice.

items.title: Q8 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Which among the following writers once remarked that “I awoke one morning and found myself famous”?
items.explanation: Lord Byron made this famous remark to his biographer Thomas Moore after the publication of Cantos I and II of Childe Harold's Pilgrimage in March 1812 brought him instantaneous international celebrity.

D. Comus
E. L’Allegro
items.explanation: In order of composition and publication: L'Allegro was written around 1631 (E), the masque Comus in 1634 (D), the pastoral elegy Lycidas in 1637 (C), the epic Paradise Lost in 1667 (A), and Paradise Regained in 1671 (B). This gives the sequence E, D, C, A, B.

items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem: Which of the following texts deals with the theme of creolisation?
items.explanation: Jean Rhys's Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) explores the cultural, racial, and psychological complexities of Caribbean creolisation through Antoinette Cosway, a white Creole heiress rejected by both white Europeans and Black Jamaicans.

items.title: Q12 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem:
List – I (Term)
A. Anaphoric word
B. Morpheme
C. Antecedent
D. Periphrasis
List – II (Definition)
I. A unit of language that cannot be analysed into smaller units.
II. Refers back to a word or phrase previously used in a text/conversation.
III. Use of two or more words to express a meaning which could otherwise be expressed in a single word.
IV. A word or phrase that is referred back to by a pronoun or other proform.
items.explanation: An anaphoric word refers back to an antecedent previously introduced in discourse (A-II); a morpheme is the smallest indivisible meaningful grammatical unit in language (B-I); an antecedent is the original referent that a pronoun subsequently refers back to (C-IV); and periphrasis is circumlocution, using multiple words where a single word would suffice (D-III).

items.title: Q13 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: The poetic line “’Tis better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all” appears in
options: S.T. Coleridge’s “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner”
Shakespeare’s “Let Me Not to the Marriage of True Minds”
items.explanation: This famous philosophical consolation occurs in Section 27 of Alfred, Lord Tennyson's great Victorian elegy In Memoriam A.H.H. (1850), written over seventeen years in grief for his Cambridge friend Arthur Henry Hallam.

items.title: Q14 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
In the 1985 essay, “Three Women’s Texts and a critique of Imperialism”, Gayatri Spivak shows development of the white liberal feminist subject. Which are the texts referred in the title of essay?
A. The Wide Sargasso Sea by Jean Rhys
B. Jane Eyre by Charlotte Bronte
C. Frankenstein by Mary Shelley
D. Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen
E. The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot
items.explanation: In her seminal 1985 essay "Three Women's Texts and a Critique of Imperialism", Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak analyzes Jean Rhys's Wide Sargasso Sea, Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre, and Mary Shelley's Frankenstein (A, B, and C) to demonstrate how 19th-century white feminist individualist heroines were shaped through colonialist assumptions. Austen's and Eliot's novels are not among the three texts studied.

items.title: Q15 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Barbara Smith, in her essay, “Toward a Black Feminist Criticism”, raises concerns for:
A. Only Black women
B. Black lesbian women
C. Black women in the White world only
D. Black lesbian women amongst black women vis-a-vis the White women
E. Black and White women, both together, as they have universal concerns
items.explanation: In "Toward a Black Feminist Criticism" (1977), Barbara Smith critiques mainstream literary criticism for erasing Black female writers, paying particular attention to the unique oppression faced by Black lesbian women (B) and situating their struggles both within Black communities and in contrast to white-dominated feminist movements (D). Statements A and E contradict her intersectional framework.

items.stem: Who among the following was not associated with Cambridge School of Critics?
items.explanation: Kenneth Burke was an influential American literary theorist and philosopher of language known for his theories of dramatism and symbolic action. F.R. Leavis, Q.D. Leavis, and William Empson were leading figures of the English Cambridge School associated with I.A. Richards and the journal Scrutiny.

A. Imagism
B. Impressionism
C. Absurdism
D. Futurism
E. Pre-Raphaelitism
items.explanation: The chronological order of emergence is: Pre-Raphaelitism in 1848 (E), Impressionism in the 1870s (B), Futurism launched by Marinetti in 1909 (D), Imagism pioneered around 1912 by Ezra Pound and H.D. (A), and the Theatre of the Absurd emerging in the 1950s (C). This yields E, B, D, A, C.

items.title: Q18 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Who among the following was not a proponent of Oxford Movement ?
items.explanation: Charles Kingsley was a Broad Church Anglican rector and Christian Socialist who strongly opposed the High Church Tractarianism of the Oxford Movement, even sparking Newman's Apologia Pro Vita Sua with his polemical attacks. John Henry Newman, Richard Hurrell Froude, and Edward Bouverie Pusey were the movement's primary leaders.

items.explanation: D.H. Lawrence's novels were published chronologically as: The White Peacock in 1911 (D), Sons and Lovers in 1913 (B), The Rainbow in 1915 (C), The Plumed Serpent in 1926 (E), and Lady Chatterley's Lover in 1928 (A). This gives the sequence D, B, C, E, A.

items.explanation: Terry Eagleton is a prominent British Marxist literary theorist and critic based in the UK, unattached to the Yale deconstructive group. The Yale School consisted of American literary critics Paul de Man, Harold Bloom, Geoffrey Hartman, J. Hillis Miller, and visiting French philosopher Jacques Derrida.

items.stem: Who among the following was not associated with Cockney School of Poetry?
items.explanation: The derogatory label "Cockney School of Poetry" was coined by John Gibson Lockhart in Blackwood's Magazine in 1817 to attack Leigh Hunt and his circle, including John Keats, William Hazlitt, and occasionally P.B. Shelley. William Blake was an older, independent visionary Romantic poet never linked to this group.

A. Australian of the Year (1973)
B. Pulitzer Prize (1965)
C. Booker Prize (1955)
D. Nobel Prize in Literature (1973)
E. Perkins Prize in Narrative (1992)
items.explanation: In 1973, Patrick White was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature (becoming the first and only Australian Nobel laureate in literature) and was also named Australian of the Year (A and D). The Pulitzer Prize is awarded only to American writers, and the Booker Prize was established in 1969.

items.explanation: Amitav Ghosh's novels were published in the following chronological order: The Circle of Reason in 1986 (E), The Shadow Lines in 1988 (B), The Calcutta Chromosome in 1995 (D), The Hungry Tide in 2004 (A), and Sea of Poppies in 2008 (C). This yields the sequence E, B, D, A, C.

items.title: Q29 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Choose the correct statements with regard to the binary pair Langue and Parole introduced by Ferdinand de Saussure
A. Langue is translated as speech and parole as language
B. Langue is the internal structure of a language not language itself.
C. Parole is the event of language.
D. Parole and language are a set of vocabulary only
E. There is no distinction between Parole and Langue
items.explanation: In Ferdinand de Saussure's structural linguistics, langue refers to the abstract, underlying rule-governed system and structure of a language (B), while parole refers to the concrete, individualized speech acts and actual events of language use (C). Statement A is incorrect because langue means language/system and parole means speech.

items.title: Q30 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)

items.stem: Which of the following writers remarked that “You are your best thing” ?
options: George Eliot in The Mill on the Floss
Arundhati Roy in The God of small things
items.explanation: This comforting declaration is spoken by Paul D to Sethe in the poignant closing chapter of Toni Morrison's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel Beloved (1987), reassuring her of her own intrinsic self-worth: "You your best thing, Sethe. You are."

items.explanation: Frantz Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks was published in 1952 (C), Edward Said's Orientalism in 1978 (A), Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o's Decolonising the Mind in 1986 (D), Homi Bhabha's edited volume Nation and Narration in 1990 (B), and Bhabha's The Location of Culture in 1994 (E). items.explanation: John Keats dedicated his mythological romance Endymion (1818) with the inscription "Inscribed to the Memory of Thomas Chatterton," commemorating the brilliant 18th-century poet who died by suicide in poverty at age seventeen.

items.title: Q37 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Who among the following was not associated with the Movement Poetry?
items.explanation: Charles Kingsley was a Victorian novelist and clergyman (1819–1875). The Movement was a 1950s British group of anti-romantic poets featuring Donald Davie, Elizabeth Jennings, John Wain, Philip Larkin, and Thom Gunn, anthologized in Robert Conquest's New Lines (1956).

items.title: Q38 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
List – I (Term)
A. Aporia
B. Énoncé
C. Encomium
D. Hagiography
List – II (Definition)
I. Technical term in structuralist theory that implies “utterance”
II. Formal eulogy in prose or verse to glorify people, objects, or ideas
III. The writing or study of the lives of the saints
IV. A term used in theory of deconstruction to indicate conflict between rhetoric thought
items.explanation: In deconstruction, aporia designates an internal contradiction or rhetorical impasse that destabilizes a text's logic (A-IV); énoncé is the structuralist term for a concrete utterance or statement (B-I); an encomium is a formal composition or speech of high praise (C-II); and hagiography denotes the biographical study and writing of the lives of saints (D-III).

items.title: Q41 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)

Identify the author who stated the following lines –
“There is, first, the literature of knowledge; and, secondly, the literature of power. The function of the first is — to teach; the function of the second is — to move : the first is a rudder, the second an oar or a sail.”
items.explanation: Thomas De Quincey formulated the celebrated distinction between the "literature of knowledge" (which conveys didactic instruction) and the "literature of power" (which moves human emotions and sensibility) in his 1848 critical review essay on Alexander Pope.

Which articles of Indian Constitution pertain to the provisions relating to the Official Language of the Union?
A. 342
B. 343
C. 344
D. 345
E. 346
items.explanation: Under Part XVII (Chapter I) of the Indian Constitution, titled "Language of the Union", Article 343 provides for the official language of the Union (Hindi in Devanagari script) and Article 344 provides for the Commission and Committee of Parliament on official language (B and C). Articles 345 and 346 govern regional and inter-state official languages.

items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: The poem “O Captain! My Captain!” is a tribute to :
items.explanation: Walt Whitman wrote the celebrated 1865 rhymed elegy "O Captain! My Captain!" to mourn the assassination of President Abraham Lincoln, depicting Lincoln as the ship's brave captain who died just as the Union survived the storm of the American Civil War.

items.explanation: The City Heiress (1682) is a Restoration comedy of manners written by Aphra Behn. The Castle of Perseverance, Mind, Will and Understanding (also called Wisdom), and Mankind are the three famous 15th-century medieval English morality plays preserved in the Macro Manuscript.

items.title: Q49 · June 2024 (Paper II - Cancelled Exam)

items.explanation: This famous maxim is stated by Samuel Johnson in his Preface to Shakespeare (1765), where Johnson argues that literature endures across centuries only when it faithfully mirrors universal human nature and general truth rather than transient local customs.

items.stem:
Which of the following definitions of linguistic terms are correct?
A. Orthoepy is the study of correct grammar in conformity with established regional patterns.
B. Philology is the study of phonemes and other characteristics of the systems of speech sounds in individual languages.
C. Synchronic study pertains to study of language at a specific historical point
D. Diachronic study pertains to historical dimensions of language i.e., linguistic change over the period of time.
E. Phonology is the study of language in its cultural and social contexts.
items.explanation: In modern linguistics, synchronic analysis examines a language's system at a particular fixed moment in time (C), while diachronic analysis investigates how languages evolve and change across historical time (D). Orthoepy is the study of correct pronunciation (not grammar), and phonology studies the sound systems of languages (whereas sociolinguistics examines social and cultural contexts).

Matthew Arnold in The Study of Poetry

This establishes the order B, D, A, C, E.

List – II (Definition)
I. Clause expressing the condition
II. Clause expressing the consequence
III. Links the subject of a sentence with a complement
IV. A pair or group of words that are habitually juxtaposed
items.explanation: In conditional syntax, the apodosis is the main clause expressing the result or consequence (A-II) and the protasis is the subordinate clause expressing the condition (B-I); a collocation is a habitual pairing of words that co-occur naturally (C-IV); and a copular verb connects the subject to a subject complement (D-III).

B. Leon Damas didn’t participate in the negritude movement.
C. Creole writers attacked this term for its monolithic look.
D. Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka considered ‘negritude’ as an unhealthy fetishism of the ‘native’ state.

items.explanation: Creole theorists such as Jean Bernabé, Patrick Chamoiseau, and Raphaël Confiant critiqued Négritude for postulating a totalizing, monolithic Black identity (C), while Wole Soyinka famously criticized Négritude as a defensive and narcissistic fetishization of racial identity (D). Which of the following statements are correct about Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s “Annihilation of Caste” and concerns dealt within it?

B. It focuses on the need to create a society where individuals are treated with dignity, respect, regardless of their caste.
C. There will be outcastes even if the caste system is completely destroyed.
D. Ideal society will always have a strong caste system even if it is based on liberty, equality and fraternity.
E. This is a fictitious novel.
items.explanation: Annihilation of Caste was originally drafted in 1936 as an undelivered presidential address for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal conference in Lahore before Ambedkar self-published it as a treatise (A).
